extracted.intended_audience: readers and critics of American literature; educated public interested in culture, poetry, and national character
extracted.subtask_description: Critical-essay criteria about what American poetry, literature, and society ought to be: standards for poetic form, authenticity, national identity, and the social conditions that nourish literature. Primarily a 19th-century cultural-literary critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality / American Totality
rubrics_metrics.description: The main sustenance for highest separate personality in the States must come from 'that general sustenance of the aggregate' — a fused, fervent identity of the individual with the idea and fact of AMERICAN TOTALITY, absorb'd in the blood and belief of the People everywhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster a cohesive national conviction (in literature, art, and life) so that individuality flourishes within a strong democratic Union; literature should emanate and reinforce this national faith (the Flag, stars and stripes) across regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of Union and State Sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two distinct principles — the sacred principle of the Union (ensemble) and the sacred principle of each State's separate sovereignty — both are necessary and must be harmoniously adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid absolutizing either centralization or state independence; cultural and political health requires preserving and reconciling both principles as complementary forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Against literary artificiality — prefer organic growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Emerson's pages are 'perhaps too perfect, too concentrated' and 'always a make, never an unconscious growth' — likened to a 'porcelain figure' rather than the real animal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued literature should feel like unconscious growth and genuine life, not an overpolished artificial product; authenticity and spontaneity trump mere refinement and learned decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of passion and imagination over cold intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: Emerson is criticized as dominated by 'cold and bloodless intellectuality' rather than passion, imagination, or 'fire' — leading to works useful as stages but not as ultimate solace in deepest hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-class poetry and literature must supply vitalizing, emotional, imaginal power — not mere abstruse intellection; seek works that move and sustain the soul, not just the mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of manners — include the picturesque 'bad manners'
rubrics_metrics.description: To the real artist in humanity, 'what are called bad manners are often the most picturesque and significant of all.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not sanitize or over-domesticate characters and social detail; literature should permit roughness and the vividness of real life rather than impose only genteel propriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic authenticity tied to the poet's life
rubrics_metrics.description: Poems of the first class 'are to be sternly tallied with the poets themselves, and tried by them and their lives.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess great poems by the integrity and life of their authors — thematic congruence between subject and author's character/moral standing matters (e.g., courage shouldn't be sung by a coward).

rubrics_metrics.name: Break down forms between prose and poetry / endorse free verse
rubrics_metrics.description: The time has arrived 'to essentially break down the barriers of form between prose and poetry' — greatest poetry 'can never again... be express'd in arbitrary and rhyming metre.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace freer, non-rhyming, rhythmic forms that fit modern subjects; allow prose-like flexibility while retaining subtle rhythm; traditional rhyme/metre may remain for lesser uses but shouldn't constrain highest expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry must address concrete American facts and modern life
rubrics_metrics.description: In these States, poetry 'will have to do with actual facts, with the concrete States' and with 'the dignity and heroism of the practical labor of farms, factories, foundries, workshops, mines, or on shipboard.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetry should reflect contemporary American realities (technology, labor, national formation) and help define the nation's artistic character; lofty themes must include the practical heroism of ordinary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Great poets require great audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: To have great poets, there must be great audiences, too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural cultivation and broad, appreciative readerships are prerequisites for producing enduring, high-quality poetry; educational and social conditions that build audiences matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: British literature not a democratic model
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'spirit of English literature' is criticized as often 'material, sensual, not spiritual... cold, anti-democratic,' with Shakespeare seen as 'incarnated, uncompromising feudalism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: American writers should not uncritically adopt British models; instead draw broadly from continental and older sources while prioritizing democratic, expansive, and life-affirming qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broaden literary sources beyond Britain (value continental and Oriental literatures)
rubrics_metrics.description: American students should 'overhaul the well-freighted fleets' of literatures of Italy, Spain, France, Germany, and rejoice in Oriental researches and poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek richer translations and study non-British literatures to supply freedom, self-possession, subtlety and other qualities lacking in English models; diversify literary influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Darwinism: adopt but temper its dominance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution (Darwinism) is 'so needed as a counterpoise' and will better and broaden erudition, but 'will have to abate its vehemence' and take its place among many theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate evolutionary insights into culture and thought, but avoid allowing any single scientific theory to monopolize metaphysical or poetic interpretation; keep plurality of perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priests and poets must recast old materials into new moulds
rubrics_metrics.description: Priests and poets must 'recast the old metal, the already achiev'd material, into and through new moulds' fully absorbing the results of modern science and democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spiritual and poetic leaders should integrate contemporary knowledge and scientific advances into renewed metaphysical and artistic expressions suitable for modern America.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject aristocratic imitation in American 'society'
rubrics_metrics.description: American attempts to imitate foreign courts and salon manners produce a comic, ill-placed fashion; we should not prefer a 'plan of a select class' that chokes the true plan for America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate social forms and manners suited to democratic life: prioritize practical virtues (farmers, sailors, mechanics, good citizens) over aristocratic refinement and snobbery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the Poverty Question and labor relations to avert unrest
rubrics_metrics.description: The core pressing issue is 'the treatment of working-people by employers' and the broader 'Poverty Question' — unchecked poverty and miserably-waged populations can produce social upheaval akin to great strikes or revolutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend policy, economic organization, wages, and social spirit: prevent growing economic inequality and misery to safeguard democracy and social peace; the state and society must respond to labor conditions.
